request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched total": the due-totals of the people the signed-in user watches, added up, or 0.00 when they watch no one. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

This only needed a front-end change. The app already stored who each user watches and sent it to the page with each person, so nothing changed in the data, the server or the audit records.

- **`features/people/people.ts`**: a new `watchedDueTotal` adds up the due-totals, as each person's row shows them, of everyone the user watches. It reuses `sumDues`, the same adding-up the other header totals use, so "n/a" values are skipped.
- **`features/header/header.ts`**: shows that figure under the `watched-due-total` test id, next to the other "My …" totals.
